issues.description: Inner blocking read loop has no timeout or process-exit backstop, trading truncation for potential deadlock.
issues.detail: After switching to blocking mode, the outer loop's timeout and check_process_exited safeguards no longer apply. If a writer hangs without closing the FIFO (stuck child, inherited fd in grandchild), the parent blocks forever. The POSIX EOF guarantee assumes all writers close — that precondition is unverified. Restore a timeout/exit-check backstop on the blocking path.

issues.description: fcntl mode switch has no error handling and no try/finally to restore fd state.
issues.detail: F_GETFL/F_SETFL can raise OSError, and there is no cleanup on the exception path. If the inner read loop raises, the fd is silently left in blocking mode for any subsequent reuse or inheritor. Wrap in try/finally that restores the original flags, or extract a helper that owns the mode transition.

issues.description: BlockingIOError handler reduced to silent pass with has_blocking_error tracking dropped.
issues.detail: After the rewrite, the except branch can only fire before any data arrives and now does nothing, while has_blocking_error semantics disappeared. Either delete the except entirely (poll already gates readiness) or add a comment justifying it as defensive. Don't leave vestigial control flow that quietly changes behavior.

issues.description: No regression test added for an intermittent race condition fix.
issues.detail: The original bug was intermittent JSON truncation at 86KB — exactly the kind of race that regresses under refactor. A deterministic fixture that writes a large payload and closes the writer fast would convert the prose proof into evidence and prevent re-breakage. Add the test before merge.

issues.description: Patch bundles the race fix with deletion of a macOS-specific workaround without justification.
issues.detail: The deleted block existed precisely because POSIX FIFO behavior wasn't observed on macOS. The commit claims POSIX guarantees subsume it but provides no evidence. Either prove the new approach handles the macOS case (with a test) or split the cleanup into a separate patch.

issues.description: Two parallel read loops where one would do; extract a drain helper and document the two phases.
issues.detail: The function has an outer non-blocking poll loop and an inner blocking drain loop, both appending to content and both deciding EOF. Extract _drain_blocking(fifo_fd) -> bytes and add a docstring naming the two phases (poll-until-first-byte, then blocking-drain-to-EOF). Makes the shape obvious and prevents someone re-introducing non-blocking drain.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is correct and the two-phase poll-then-blocking-drain strategy is the right shape, but the execution is under-engineered. The dominant concern (P0) is that the inner blocking read loop discards every safety net — no timeout, no process-exit check, no fcntl error handling — so an intermittent truncation has been traded for a potential indefinite hang if any writer fails to close. Secondary concerns: the fd mode change has no try/finally, the BlockingIOError handler became a silent pass, a macOS workaround was deleted without justification, and no regression test reproduces the 86KB truncation. Recommend NEEDS-WORK: add the backstop, guard the fd state, justify or restore the macOS handling, and add a deterministic test before merge.
